title: Orchestrator Release-Evidence Work: Build Paths, Completeness, and Necessity

tldr.content: The five-item list is necessary but stale and incomplete. Items 1-3 are substantially satisfied in committed code and green required CI; what remains there is three narrow residual enforcement defects plus record closure. Items 4-5 (independent final review, parent-plan reconciliation) are genuinely open and are the real release gates. The list omits: exact-SHA binding of the closure commit + rollback checkpoint, a changelog/version record, required-check configuration verification, and the (user-gated) publication path. Revised work list: 4 residual code fixes, run the built-but-never-run independent final review at the release SHA, build one outcome-parity live test, reconcile all stale records, then close with exact-SHA CI evidence.

executiveSummary.content:
Four parallel read-only researchers examined the repository's plans, checkpoints, code, CI workflow, and external release-engineering standards (NIST SP 800-53 SA-11/CM-4, NIST SSDF PS.3.2/PW.7, SLSA provenance, Google SRE release engineering). Headline correction: the plan records predate the code. The persisted-review enforcement (commits b6f2843/f636c80/0c99e5a) landed AFTER the lean-mvp plan was checkpointed BLOCKED, and the composed orchestrator-to-browse and orchestrator-to-Docker live proofs exist (scripts/adapter-required-tests.mjs:188-195) and run green zero-skip in required CI (runs 33903446355, 33928035357). Convergence across three independent tracks on the same residual defects gives high confidence in the revised list.

```text
5-item candidate list -> 4-track DEEP research -> verdict per item
  items 1-3: REQUIRED but ~satisfied (3 residual defects + record closure)
  items 4-5: REQUIRED and genuinely OPEN (the real gates)
  + 4 missing items pulled in (exact-SHA closure, changelog, required-check, publication)
```

keyFindings.content:
1. KF1 (necessity, supported, high): All five candidate items map to recognized release-engineering/assurance practice — NIST SP 800-53 SA-11 (test evidence, independent agent verification), CM-4(1) (operational-environment validation), SSDF PS.3.2 (release provenance) and PW.7 (review before release), SLSA provenance, SRE release engineering (exact-branch test reruns, change reports, rollback).
2. KF2 (staleness, supported, high): Items 1-3 are substantially SATISFIED in committed code and green required CI. The lean-mvp plan's two blockers were cured by b6f2843 (persisted review enforcement) and the composed live proofs; plan records predate the fixes. Caveat: the green run is pinned to 0ec452a, not HEAD 368d5bb — the 9 intervening commits touch no adapter-lane files, but exact-SHA closure still requires a fresh green run at the release SHA.
3. KF3 (residual defect A, supported, high): The browse live proof still builds its evidence resolver with requireSourceDigest:false (tests/orchestrate-browse-live-integration.test.mjs:96-101, :363-368), and the browse adapter never passes expectedSourceDigest in its resolve call (csm-orchestrate/lib/csm-browse-adapter.mjs:294-302) — the PNG-to-record lineage bind is by construction, not resolver-enforced.
4. KF4 (residual defect B, supported after downgrade, high): The host-adapter review seam skips the index-level 3-ref persisted-record validation (including per-ref sourceDigest binding) and the adversarial-review/2 + final-review/2 schema asserts (csm-orchestrate/lib/index.mjs:1601, 1614, 1630, 1662) because the gate is (finalReviewExecutor || hostReview.reviewArtifactRefs) and invocation.mjs invokeReview returns without reviewArtifactRefs; however invocation.mjs:727-742 still resolver-validates each receipt/artifact record and fails closed if the resolver is missing — what is skipped is the index-layer triple validation, not all persisted-record validation.
5. KF5 (parity, supported, high): No live standalone-adapter-vs-orchestrated outcome comparison exists anywhere (grep: only plan/research text). The repo's canonical parity idiom (lib/rollout/shadow.mjs canonicalize + assertZeroSideEffects) is not applied to adapter orchestration. This is the substance of lean-mvp T004's 'outcome parity'.
6. KF6 (assurance, supported, high): The independent final-review machinery is fully built (adversarial-final-review.mjs: identity separation, authoritative re-derivation, 0600 persisted records, reviewArtifactRefs) but has never been run and recorded for a RELEASE decision: every active release plan has completionReview:null (the one filled completionReview, 2026-09-04-replace-npm-audit-ci-gate-csm.json:503, is a CI-gate plan); the newest review artifact in .agents/reviews/ is 2026-08-30 at commit 75adabe, pre-dating substantial orchestrator work.
7. KF7 (reconciliation, supported, high): Stale falsified blockers persist across at least 5 plans + build states (adapter-variables-unset, runner-image, npm-audit-timeout, E2E 14/89, sandbox-unavailable — all cured); .agents/README.md index lines drift from plan JSON state; 2026-08-27-csm-orchestrate-csm.json is malformed JSON (missing comma ~line 359) and cannot be parsed at all.
8. KF8 (completeness, partially-supported, high): The list is NOT complete. Verified omissions: (a) exact-SHA binding of the final closure commit + rollback descriptor (lean-mvp AC5, ci-blockers-followup T003); (b) version/changelog record for the only versioned release unit @jamiemills/csm-skills-bootstrap@0.1.0 (no CHANGELOG exists); (c) required-check configuration for the Adapter integrations job (not locally inspectable, unrecorded); (d) publication path DEF-RELEASE (npm publish/sign/replay — user-gated, open); (e) scheduled dependency audits (schedule: trigger absent).
9. KF9 (scope boundary, context-dependent, high): Deployment/autonomy gates G2/G3/G5-G8 (docs/production-readiness-report.md verdict NOT READY FOR AUTONOMY) gate autonomy promotion, not release-evidence closure. Different bar; do not silently fold in, but state the distinction in the release record.
10. KF10 (record hygiene, upheld, high): .agents/csm-build-state/replace-npm-audit-ci-gate-20260904.json contains a duplicate journal key (lines 27 and 49); parsers silently keep only the last entry, shadowing the run's recovery journal. Fold into the reconciliation work item.
11. KF11 (test coverage, upheld, high): All outcome-corpus negative tests for review tampering exercise only the finalReviewExecutor seam (tests/orchestrate-outcome-corpus.test.mjs:379, 507-530); the host seam (adapter.invokeReview, index.mjs:1560) has no equivalent persisted-record negative coverage — reinforces KF4's fix needing its own corpus negatives.

detailSections.content:
R1-residual: (1) drop requireSourceDigest:false from tests/orchestrate-browse-live-integration.test.mjs:100 and :367 (static analysis says records already satisfy default enforcement; if not, switch harness to taxonomy helpers as adversarial-final-review.mjs:420-424 does); (2) add expectedSourceDigest: native.digest to csm-browse-adapter.mjs resolve call (:294-302); (3) mirror to payload copies (check-suite.mjs:800-801 parity gate); acceptance = production-evidence-boundaries T001 signal re-run + raw E2E stays 89/89.
R2-residual: (1) make invokeReview persist the full review record set and return reviewArtifactRefs (reuse persistReviewRecords shape); (2) change index.mjs:1601/1614 to require validation whenever hostReview.status==='completed' && hostReview.review; (3) add expectedSourceDigest to host-seam resolver calls (mirroring index.mjs:375); (4) extend orchestrate-outcome-corpus.test.mjs:505-538 with a reviewRecordPaths-only-executor negative + host-seam-with-refs positive; (5) expect test-host updates at the six known host implementations (telemetry-wiring:171, autonomy:158, autonomy-e2e:163, recovery-sqlite:154, e2e:172, helpers-final-review:117). Fail direction is BLOCKED/REQUIRES_REVIEW, never false-VERIFIED.
Parity: new tests/orchestrate-outcome-parity.test.mjs (skip-gated on CSM_ADAPTER_INTEGRATIONS_REQUIRED=1) comparing standalone adapter.execute vs orchestrate() on deterministic projections only (status, effects, metrics, cleanup, digest shapes — never raw receipts/timestamps), using canonicalize from lib/schema-runtime; include a blocked-path parity case; append to ADAPTER_REQUIRED_TEST_FILES in scripts/adapter-required-tests.mjs:188-191.
Assurance: run createIndependentFinalReviewExecutor with genuinely distinct producer/reviewer identities against the release corpus at HEAD; persist the three records under .agents/ evidence storage (not tmp); confirm every reviewArtifactRefs entry resolves via production resolver; record completionReview + rollback descriptor; the review scope must include a current-SHA security look at the orchestrator's command/secret surface (SSDF PW.7), superseding the 2026-08-30/75adabe review.
Reconciliation: scripts/close-plan.mjs exists for closure; fix the malformed 2026-08-27 plan JSON; clear falsified blockers with run 33903446355/33928035357 evidence; sync .agents/README.md index; lean-mvp AC1 demands 'no stale blocked claims remain in the active cursor'.

recommendation.content: Replace the stale five-item list with a nine-item ordered work list: (1) R1 residual — strict resolver defaults in the browse live test + expectedSourceDigest bind in csm-browse-adapter; (2) R2 residual — host-seam reviewArtifactRefs emission + unconditional completed-review validation + corpus negatives (including the currently-missing host-seam tampering cases); (3) build the outcome-parity live test and add it to the required adapter lane; (4) run the independent final review at the release SHA (scope includes current-SHA security surface; producer/reviewer identity separation is mandatory; record the in-process-vs-process-isolation governance caveat in the residual-risk register); (5) create the changelog/version record for @jamiemills/csm-skills-bootstrap@0.1.0; (6) reconcile ALL stale records (5+ plans, build states, README index, malformed 2026-08-27 JSON, duplicate journal key in replace-npm-audit-ci-gate build state) — lean-mvp AC1 makes this a gate, not hygiene; (7) verify the Adapter integrations job is a required check (external, GitHub settings); (8) close the parent plan via scripts/close-plan.mjs with exact-SHA green CI (closure commit needs its own green run) + rollback descriptor; (9) hold DEF-RELEASE publication and autonomy gates G5-G8 as explicitly separate, user-owned decisions. Validation questions: will tightening index.mjs:1601 break the six known host implementations (test updates expected, fail-closed direction); is requireSourceDigest:false strictly removable (static analysis says yes; verify by running the acceptance signal). What would change the recommendation: discovery that host-seam reviews were intentionally exempt (would downgrade KF4 to accepted-deviation and require a recorded security rationale).

unverifiedClaims.content:
- requireSourceDigest:false removability in the browse live test is derived analytically from digest-taxonomy math, not executed (T2, medium confidence).
- Whether host-seam invokeReview was intentionally exempt from ref enforcement is unknown (T2 medium; check b6f2843 review history).
- Branch-protection required-check status of the Adapter integrations job is not locally inspectable (T1 medium).
- Whether tightening index.mjs:1601 breaks the six known host tests is predicted but unexecuted (T2); the fix is fail-closed by direction (BLOCKED/REQUIRES_REVIEW, never false-VERIFIED).
- In-process final-review independence is governance-level, not process isolation (prior research, carried into residual-risk register).
- CI run evidence for 89/89 E2E and 11/11 docker tests is cited from plan/build-state records, not re-fetched from GitHub Actions API in this run.
- Whether the host-seam review bypass was intentional (accepted deviation) or accidental is unresolved from code alone — check b6f2843 review history before fixing KF4.
- Green required-adapter run 33903446355 is pinned to 0ec452a; HEAD 368d5bb has no own green full-run record (9 intervening commits touch no adapter-lane files).
